questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding large dams?

I. They have social problems because they displace large number of peasants and tribals without adequate compensation or rehabilitation.

II. They have Environmental problems because they contribute enormously to deforestation and the loss of biological diversity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2) Both I and II.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Understanding the statements in relation to large dams**

__
 
• **Social Problems**

 
 
• Large dams have significant social impacts, particularly on the lives of peasants and tribal communities.
 
• The construction of large dams often necessitates the displacement of large populations from their ancestral lands.
 
• Many affected individuals and communities face inadequate compensation and lack proper rehabilitation plans.* Hence statement I is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Environmental Problems**
 
 
• The construction and operation of large dams can have profound environmental consequences.
 
• They often lead to extensive deforestation, which in turn reduces biodiversity by destroying habitats.
 
• This loss of forests and biological diversity can disrupt local ecosystems and contribute to larger environmental issues.* Hence statement II is correct.*
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Impacts on Local Communities**

 
 
• The construction of large dams can disrupt local economies that are dependent on traditional practices and occupations.
 
• The disruption can lead to long-term socio-economic challenges for the displaced populations.
 
 
 
• **Hydrological Changes**
 
 
• Large dams alter the natural flow of rivers, which can impact the water availability downstream.
 
• These hydrological changes can negatively affect agriculture, fisheries, and the natural sediment transport, leading to further environmental degradation.

__
 
• In India, the primary financial institution that protects investors in the stock market is the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).**
 
• **SEBI** is a regulatory body that was established in 1988 to protect the interests of investors in the Indian securities market and to promote the development of the securities market.
 
• **SEBI **regulates and supervises the activities of various market participants, including stock exchanges, brokers, mutual funds, and other intermediaries, and it also enforces rules and regulations related to trading, disclosure, and transparency in the securities market.
 
• **SEBI** plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity and stability of the Indian securities market and in safeguarding the interests of investors by ensuring fair and transparent trading practices, promoting investor education and awareness, and enforcing laws and regulations to prevent fraud and malpractice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is a major stock exchange located in Mumbai, India**.

 
 
• It was established in **1875**, making it one of the oldest stock exchanges in **Asia.**
 
• The **BSE** is a popular platform for trading in stocks, bonds, and other financial instruments, and it is known for its role in shaping the Indian capital market.
 
• The **BSE** has a market capitalization of over $2 trillion, making it one of the largest stock exchanges in the world.
 
• The **BSE** also serves as an important source of financing for Indian companies, allowing them to raise capital by issuing stocks and bonds to investors.
 
• The **BSE** is regulated by the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), **which is responsible for ensuring fair and transparent trading practices in the Indian securities market.
 
• The** BSE** has played a significant role in the growth and development of the Indian economy, and it continues to be a major hub for investment and trading activity in India.
 
 
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India, responsible for regulating the monetary policy of the country and supervising the banking system.**
 
 
• The **RBI **was established in **1935 **and is headquartered in** Mumbai.** Its main functions include formulating and implementing monetary policy, regulating and supervising banks and other financial institutions, managing the foreign exchange market, and issuing currency.
 
• The **RBI** is governed by a central board of directors, headed by a Governor who is appointed by the Indian government.
 
• The **RBI** plays a crucial role in maintaining financial stability and promoting economic growth in India.
 
• Its policies and decisions have a significant impact on the banking and financial sectors in the country, as well as on the broader economy.
 
• The **RBI **also serves as a lender of last resort, providing liquidity to banks and other financial institutions in times of crisis.
 
 
 
• **The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is one of the major stock exchanges in India, located in Mumbai.**
 
 
• It was established in **1992** and has since become one of the largest stock exchanges in the world by market capitalization.
 
• The **NSE** provides a platform for trading in a wide range of financial instruments, including equities, futures and options, currencies, and debt securities. It is known for its advanced electronic trading platform and has been a pioneer in introducing technology-driven innovations in the Indian securities market.
 
• The** NSE** is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and operates under strict rules and regulations to ensure fair and transparent trading practices.
 
• The **NSE **has played a significant role in the development of the Indian capital market, providing investors with access to a wide range of investment opportunities and contributing to the growth and development of Indian businesses.
 
• The **NSE **has also been a driving force behind the growth of the Indian economy and has helped to promote economic stability and growth by facilitating the flow of capital to businesses and entrepreneurs.

questions.question: Which of the following colloid is an example of foam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sponge is a type of colloid** in which gas is dispersed in a **solid, rather than in a liquid**.
 
• In a sponge, **a solid material (such as cellulose or polyurethane) forms a network of pores that trap gas.**
 
• When a sponge is **soaked in water,** the pores fill with water and create a stable suspension.
 
• This is different from a foam, where gas is dispersed in a **liquid.**
 
• An example of a sponge colloid is the **polyurethane foam used in mattresses, cushions, and insulation, in which air is dispersed within a solid polyurethane matrix.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Butter is a complex mixture of many different chemical compounds, including fats, proteins, water, and various other substances**.

 
 
• The major chemical components of butter are the fatty acids, which are long chains of **carbon and hydrogen atoms.**
 
• The **fatty acids **in butter can vary depending on the source and processing of the butter, but they are typically a mixture of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Cheese is a complex mixture of proteins, fats, and water, as well as various vitamins, minerals, and flavor compounds.** The specific chemical form of cheese can vary depending on the type of cheese, but some of the key components include:

 
 
• 
 
**Proteins:** Cheese contains a variety of proteins, including casein and whey proteins. These proteins are made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. The specific amino acid composition of cheese can vary depending on the type of cheese and how it is made.

 
 
• 
 
**Fats:** Cheese is also high in fat, which is an important source of flavor and texture. The fats in cheese are mostly in the form of triglycerides, which are made up of fatty acids and glycerol.

 
 
• 
 
**Water:** Cheese contains varying amounts of water, depending on the type of cheese and how it is made. The water content can range from less than 40% for hard, aged cheeses to over 70% for soft, fresh cheeses.

 
 
• 
 
**Minerals:** Cheese is a good source of calcium, phosphorus, and other minerals that are important for bone health and other bodily functions.

 
 
• 
 
**Flavor compounds:** Cheese contains a wide variety of flavor compounds, including volatile compounds like esters, aldehydes, and ketones, as well as non-volatile compounds like amino acids and peptides. The specific flavor profile of cheese can vary depending on the type of cheese and how it is made.

questions.question: Which state among the following has the largest reserves of gold ore in India as of 2021?
questions.solution:

__
 
• As per **National Mineral Inventory data**, the total reserves/resources of gold ore (**primary**) in the country have been estimated at **501.83 million tonnes**.
 
• In India, largest resources of gold ore (primary) are located in **Bihar** (44%) followed by** Rajasthan** (25%), **Karnataka** (21%), **West Bengal **(3%),** Andhra Pradesh** (3% ), **Jharkhand** (2 %).
 
• The remaining **2%** resources of ore are located in** Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra,** and **Tamil Nadu**.

• Karnataka__ is the largest producer of gold in India.

• The remaining production was reported from Jharkhand.

• Karnataka has the only operational gold mine in India.
 
• Hutti Gold Mines is the only producer of primary gold in the country.
 
 
• Hutti Gold Mines has the capacity to produce 5,50,000 tonnes per annum.
 
• Hutti Gold Mine is one of the most ancient metal mines in the world.
 
 
 
• Kolar gold fields closed on 28 February 2001 due to a fall in gold prices.

• Mahi

 
 
• ​It originates in the Mahi Kanta hills, from the northern slopes of Vindhyas at an altitude of 500 m near village Bhopawar, Sardarpur Tehsil in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat, and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **​Narmada**
 
 
• The Narmada river originates from the Narmada Kund located in Amarkantak, Anuppur district in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Amarkantak is located on the Maikal mountain. 
 
• The Narmada river forms the unmarked boundary between North and South India.
 
• The major tributaries of the Narmada are Barna, Tawa, Kanar, Kolar, Man, Hatni, Uri, Shakkar, etc.
 
• It flows westwards (1, 312 km) before falling into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• The Narmada river is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh and it's called "The Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh".
 
• The waterfalls created by the Narmada River include Kapil Dhara and Dudh Dhara Falls (Anuppur), Dhuandhar Falls (Bhedaghat, Jabalpur), Sahasradhara Falls (Maheshwar, Khargone), Dardhi Falls, Manadhata Falls, etc.
 
 

 
• **Tapi**

 
 
• The Tapti River (aka Tapi river )is a river in central India located to the south of the Narmada river which flows westwards before draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river has a length of around 724 kms and flows through the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Tapti river originates from Multai Betul district Madhya Pradesh. And also from the Satpura range.

questions.question: What is used for holding program instructions that can't be changed throughout the life of the computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ROM**

 
 
• Read-Only Memory is a ROM in a computer.
 
• Read-only memory is a storage medium that permanently stores data on computers and electronic devices.
 
• The data stored in these chips is nonvolatile i.e. it is not lost when power is removed.
 
• There are five basic ROM types:
 
 
• ROM: Read-Only Memory.
 
• PROM: Programmable read-only memory.
 
• EPROM: Erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• EEPROM: Electrically erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• Flash memory: Flash memory, a type of EEPROM that uses in-circuit wiring. 
 
 
 
• BIOS uses Flash memory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Register**

 
 
• The smallest and fastest memory of a computer is registered memory located in the computer's central processing unit(CPU).
 
• It generally stores the most used instructions, data, etc. which are to be used by CPU.
 
• Control Unit is part of the CPU.
 
• It advises the input and output devices, and computer memory on how to respond to the instructions sent to the processor.
 
 
 
• **RAM**
 
 
• It stores data that the computer needs to use temporarily. So it is faster than the secondary storage devices. It is a volatile memory i.e. the data disappear from it when the power is off.
 
• It is known as the Read-Write Memory. i.e. the user can write information into RAM and read information from it.
 
• It is called random access since any memory location can be accessed randomly for reading and writing. The access time is the same for each memory location.
 
• It is usually called “temporary” memory, which means that when the system is shut down, the memory is lost.
 
 
 
• **Cache**
 
 
• A cache memory is used by the central processing unit of a computer to reduce the average cost time or energy to access data from the** main memory**. 
 
• Generally Cache memory is logically positioned between** CPU** and **main memory**.

questions.question: Which of the following comes under Union List of 7th schedule of the Indian constitution?

options.text: Establishment of standards of weight and measure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Establishment of standards of weight and measure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Seventh schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the division of powers between the union and the states in terms of the list.
 
• The Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India defines and specifies the allocation of powers and functions between Union & States.
 
• It contains three lists:

 
• Union List,
 
• State List and
 
• Concurrent List

 
• 7th Schedule of Indian Constitution – Union List had 97 subjects. Now, it has 100 subjects.
 
• 88th Amendment added a new subject in the Union List called ‘taxes on services.’
 
• The state list has 61 subjects. Earlier, it had 66 items.
 
• The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1991 made special provisions in relation to National Capital. Laws cannot be made by the Delhi government on three subjects under State List named as – Public Order, Police & Land.
 
• The concurrent list has 52 subjects enumerated under it.

questions.question: Who led the Battle of Plassey on behalf of the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Battle of Plassey:

 
 
• It was fought in 1757 in the Plassey region of West Bengal, on the east of the Bhagirathi river. 
 
• Troops of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, came up against the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• The victory of the British East India Company in the Battle of Plassey is one of the important landmarks in India History. 
 
• The Battle of Plassey paved the way for the beginning of the British empire in India.
 
• The British enjoyed the tax benefits, had to compete with no rival foreign merchants, and began to use the revenue of Bengal for protecting their military and trade interests.
 
• So much wealth was drained from Bengal that the economy was completely shattered. This is known as the Plassey Plunder.
 
• With the wealth of Bengal, the British secured their business and political supremacy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Governor and company of merchants of London trading into the East Indies, popularly known as the English East India Company, were formed in 1600 AD. 
 
• Captain William Hawkins arrived at Jahangir’s court in 1609 AD to seek permission to open a factory in Surat.
 
 
• A Farman was issued by Jahangir, permitting the English to build a factory in Surat.
 
 
 
• In 1613, a permanent factory of East India Company was established at Surat.
 
• In 1611, the company established its first factory in the south in Masulipattanam.

• Premchand

 
 
• Premchand, also known as Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, was an Indian author best known for his contemporary Hindustani writing.
 
• He was born on July 31, 1880, and died on October 8, 1936.

• He is one of the most well-known authors on the Indian continent and is recognised as one of the greatest Hindi authors of the first half of the 20th century. 
 
• He has written various novels, including, Godaan, Karmabhoomi, Gaban, Mansarovar, and Idgah.
 
• In a book titled Soz-e-Watan, he released his first collection of five short stories.

questions.question: At high doses, ______ kills cancer cells or slows their growth by damaging their DNA. Cancer cells whose DNA is damaged beyond repair stop dividing or die. When the damaged cells die, they are broken down and removed by the body.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiation therapy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Radiotherapy to treat cancer:

 
 
• High doses of radiation are used in radiation therapy, also known as radiotherapy, as a cancer treatment to eradicate cancer cells and reduce tumour size.
 
• As with X-rays of your teeth or shattered bones, radiation is utilised at low doses in x-rays to see inside your body.
 
• Radiation therapy damages cancer cells' DNA, which either kills them or limits their growth at high dosages.
 
• Cancer cells that have DNA damage that cannot be repaired either cease proliferating or die.
 
• When the injured cells expire, the body degrades and eliminates them.
 
• But too much radiation can damage tissues by changing cell structure and damaging DNA.
 
• This can cause serious health problems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemotherapy **

 
 
• Chemotherapy is the use of any drug to treat any disease.
 
• But to most people, the word chemotherapy means drugs used for** cancer treatment**. 
 
• It's often shortened to “chemo.” Surgery and radiation therapy remove, kill, or damage cancer cells in a certain area, but chemo can work throughout the whole body.
 
 

 
• Surgery:

 
 
• Surgery is a medical speciality that employs operative manual and instrumental techniques on a patient to examine or treat a pathological condition.
 
• Such as a disease or injury, to enhance bodily function or appearance, or to repair unwelcome ruptured areas
 
 
 
• **Physiotherapy**
 
 
• ​Physiotherapy is a healthcare profession that aims to help people restore and maintain movement and function when affected by** injury**, **illness** or **disability**.
 
• Physiotherapists use a combination of manual **therapy**, **exercise**, and **education**.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution is related to the writ of the High Courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Under Article 226, a writ petition can be filed in a High court for issuing one of the five writs as per the case. 
 
• A High Court is empowered to issue directions, orders, or writs for the enforcement of a Fundamental Right and for any other purpose those include:
 
 
• Habeas corpus
 
• Mandamus
 
• Prohibition
 
• Quo warranto
 
• Certiorari.
 
 
 
• The Supreme Court is considered the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights(Article 32). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution has been described as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Indian Constitution by Dr B. R. Ambedkar.

 
 
• It gives a citizen the right to approach the Supreme Court to get resorted to any of the fundamental rights in case of their violation.
 
• It is also known as the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

__

 __

• It ends on the confluence of five rivers which includes the Chambal, Kwari, Yamuna, Sind, Pahuj, at Pachnada near Bhareh in Uttar Pradesh, at the border of Bhind and Etawah districts.

• The major tributaries of the Narmada are Barna, Tawa, Kanar, Kolar, Man, Hatni, Uri, Shakkar, etc.
 
• It flows westwards before falling into the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• The Narmada river is the longest river in Madhya Pradesh and it's called "The Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh".
 
• The waterfalls created by the Narmada River include Kapil Dhara and Dudh Dhara Falls (Anuppur), Dhuandhar Falls (Bhedaghat, Jabalpur), Sahasradhara Falls (Maheshwar, Khargone), Dardhi Falls, Manadhata Falls, etc.
 
 
 
• Mahi River
 
 
• It rises in Madhya Pradesh and, after flowing through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
• It is one of Five west-flowing rivers in India, along with Tapti River, Sabarmati River, Luni River (Endorheic river) and the Narmada River.
 
• Tributaries- Som, Anas, and Panam.

questions.question: Which of the following has revamped the E-Baal Nidan online portal in September 2022?

options.text: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
Ministry of women and child development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Commission for Protection of Child Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **E-Baal Nidan **is an online complaint mechanism **launched in 2015 to enable individuals to report violations committed against a child and track them.**
 
• **It was revamped in September 2022.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was set up in March 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005, an Act of Parliament (December 2005).
 
• The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) is a statutory body under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005 under the administrative control of the Ministry of Women & Child Development, Government of India.
 
• The Commission's Mandate is to ensure that all Laws, Policies, Programmes, and Administrative Mechanisms are in consonance with the Child Rights perspective as enshrined in the Constitution of India and also the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.
 
• The Child is defined as a person in the 0 to 18 years age group.
 
• The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) works at State, Central and Local bodies. 
 
• Independent monitoring of the implementation of the Act is assigned to the National Council of Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), the main responsibilities are:
 
 
• examine and review safeguards for rights under this Act, and recommend measures for effective implementation
 
• inquire into complaints relating to child’s right to free and compulsory education
 
• conduct periodic social audits of the status of implementation and review
 
 
 
• Hence, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) works at ​State, Central and Local bodies.

questions.question: Who is famously known as the father of Indian nuclear programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Homi J. Bhabha__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Homi Jehangir Bhabha is called as father of Indian nuclear program.
 
• He is also called as Architect of the nuclear Age and Architect of the atomic bomb.
 
• He was founding director of Atomic energy establishment, Trombay (AEET) which is now named the Bhabha atomic research centre in his honor.
 
• He was the founding chairman of Atomic Energy Commission (AEC), which was established in 1948.
 
• He was awarded the Adam prize and Padma Bhushan.
 
• He was also nominated for Noble prize for physics in 1951 and 1953-56.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Sarabhai** initiated space research and helped to develop nuclear power in India.
 
• He is internationally regarded as father of Indian space program.
 
• He was the founder of Indian Space Research Organization(ISRO).
 
• APJ Abdul Kalam was an Indian aerospace scientist and known as Missile Man of India.
 
• He was intimately involved in civil space program and military missile development efforts.
 
• U.R.Rao was an Indian space scientist and former chairman of ISRO.
 
• He is known as The Satellite Man of India.
 
• **C.V. Raman **discovered the** Raman effect**, which occurs when light scatters and changes wavelength as it passes through a material. This phenomenon is now known as Raman scattering.
 
• **Venkatraman Radhakrishnan** was a physicist and radio astronomer who contributed to many areas of study, including the magnetic field of Jupiter, the rotation of Jupiter's interior, and pulsar astronomy.
